results.fact: Season window: season/itinerary.cal say Jul-Sep, but best_season/seasonal_guidance/pro_tips say the route is best (and conditions degrade badly by high summer) in Late May-early July
results.evidence: Deep retry found dated ascents across the whole year (a May 2019 forum report, a July 4-5 2014 blog ascent described as 'fine early-season shape', a November ascent narrative) and a route database noting only that the bergschrund opens late season and that a second tool and screws are needed in late season/fall; a guide service offers the peak March-October. No source states a best window for the face (neither Jul-Sep nor Late May-early July), so neither season nor best_season/seasonal_guidance is changed.

results.correct_value: The CJ Couloir approach crosses remnant Sill Glacier ice that can hold crevasses, bergschrunds and moats mid- to late season
results.evidence: Two independent accounts of the CJ Couloir describe crevasses in it: a September 2001 ascent report meets a wall-to-wall crevasse at the top of the fan (water ice, second tool needed), passes another on a steep ramp and a third bridged only in the centre, and belays from the moat at the col; a July 2014 descent report calls it a 3,500-ft snow couloir that may involve multiple crevasse/bergschrund crossings, the snow being the Sill Glacier, with a full-width crack and a bottomless moat. A 2003 ski report adds a moat and seracs on the Sill Glacier above. So seasonal_hazards.crevasses 'N/A - no glacier travel' is wrong and is replaced; obj_haz already lists crevasses.

patches.expect: N/A - no glacier travel indicated for this route; it is a couloir/ridge snow-and-rock line, not a glaciated approach (not explicitly confirmed either way in sources)
patches.value: The CJ Couloir holds remnant ice of the Sill Glacier. From mid-season on, as its snow breaks up, expect crevasses and bergschrunds that can span the full width of the couloir, plus deep moats along its edges; passing them can take steep ice moves, and the same breaks must be crossed again on the descent.

results.fact: distance to the East Ridge/col area
results.evidence: Still no mileage for the couloir approach: the 2001 and 2014 couloir accounts and a 2003 ski report describe it only as a short road walk (about a quarter mile to the hairpin), a creek crossing and ~15 minutes of brush to the fan, then about 3,400 ft of couloir to the col. A 2019 Johannesburg East Ridge report gives 10.8-14.5 mi round trip, but by the Cascade Pass/Doug's Direct line, not this couloir. The itinerary's 5.7 mi per day and dist_km 18.35 look like the Cascade Pass variant's figures, but no source states either line's one-way distance to the col, so nothing is patched.

results.fact: 'Base of west ridge' waypoint (6,800 ft, 5.2 mi) sits before the 7,100 ft camp although the ridge scrambling starts at the ~8,000 ft col above camp
results.evidence: STRUCTURAL: the 'Base of west ridge' pin (6,800 ft, distMi 5.2, coordinate 47.5575,-120.842 where the ground is ~7,308 ft) should be MOVED to the ~8,000 ft saddle between Windy Ridge and Cashmere where the ridge scramble starts (and re-elevated to ~8,000 ft with a distMi beyond the 6.5 mi camp), or else renamed as the leave-trail point (~6,700-6,900 ft, on the Windy Pass trail above Lake Caroline) and moved there. Sources: a scramble write-up says leave the Windy Pass trail at 6,700 ft, angle up to the 8,000 ft level and run the ridge to the prominent 8,000 ft saddle; a 2018 report left the trail near a ~6,900 ft meadow and reached the saddle at 8,000 ft; a 2016 report camped in Windy Basin at 6,500 ft and gained the ridge at the low saddle between Windy Ridge and Cashmere. Either fix needs a pin move, which the patch format cannot express; no text patch.

results.fact: Recommended start time from high camp — 5:00 AM vs ~6:00 AM
results.evidence: No source states a recommended departure from the high camp: a 2016 party camped in Windy Basin reached the summit 4.4 hours from camp shortly before noon (a start near 7:30-8 AM), and a 2018 party rose after 8 AM from a Lake Caroline camp; other reports are single-day pushes from the trailhead. Neither 5:00 AM nor ~06:00 is supported, and a start recommendation is a planning choice rather than a researchable fact, so nothing is patched.

results.fact: Climbing season: May-Jun header vs a season description running through September
results.evidence: Deep retry found two dated ascents of this White River / Thunder Creek southwest-face line, both in late spring: May 28-30, 1977 (rock scramble and snow climb, camp in Chalangin Basin) and June 1, 2025 (icy from an overnight freeze, crampons needed; that author waited for late May after April and November attempts failed). A November 2024 attempt on the same line turned back on wind slab 500 ft below the top, and its author describes an earlier late-October descent of the basin through open trees. These support late spring but do not state a window, and nothing found confirms or rules out a summer dry scramble (the only summer attempt, August 2023, failed on the overgrown trail), so neither season nor best_season/climate is changed.
